items.problem: Bootstrap silently omitted UWP project-linked source and assets.
items.evidence: lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[1]; source csproj linked App/MainPage/scenario XAML/styles/assets while bootstrap reported only four copied files.
items.root_cause: A directory walk under Source cannot discover external files represented by csproj Include/Link metadata.
items.change: Parse common declared UWP project item types, resolve project properties including GetDirectoryNameOfFileAbove, validate Link destinations, and materialize linked files before namespace rewrite and triage.
items.expected_effect: Agents receive the actual source XAML, code, styles, and assets and no longer reconstruct UI from generated obj artifacts.
items.falsifiable_check: Running bootstrap on this source reports project-linked files and produces App.xaml, MainPage.xaml, both scenario XAML files, Styles/Styles.xaml, and linked assets in the target.

items.problem: UserDataProtectionManager compiled but yielded fallback-only pages in WinUI desktop.
items.evidence: migration-score.json: both features fail with only the unavailable fallback; skill-defects.json item 3.
items.root_cause: The unsupported inventory lacked an AppContainer-bound API whose runtime unavailability is invisible to build and process-alive checks.
items.change: Add UserDataProtectionManager to the unsupported inventory and document why DPAPI is not a behavior-equivalent replacement for lock-state availability levels.
items.expected_effect: Affected files are explicitly deferred during bootstrap instead of being marked done while exposing no functional controls.
items.falsifiable_check: Bootstrap maps both scenario code-behind files to defer and the validator rejects retained non-deferred UserDataProtectionManager references.

items.problem: Build instructions named a nonexistent command and did not make minimum-OS reconciliation explicit.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turn 25 `winapp build` failure; turn 26 CA1416 warnings; turn 27 minimum-version correction.
items.root_cause: Prose conflated winapp launch tooling with compilation and discussed TFM without separately directing TargetPlatformMinVersion handling.
items.change: Use dotnet build consistently and strengthen the existing csproj section with a CA1416-driven TargetPlatformMinVersion rule.
items.expected_effect: The first compile command works and retained Windows APIs build without platform-compatibility warnings.
items.falsifiable_check: On rerun there is no `winapp build` invocation or unrecognized-command error, and final dotnet build reports zero CA1416 warnings.

deferred_to_human: The evaluator's original UWP capture remained on the splash frame; evaluation instruments are out of scope for this improvement.
